display.title: The Doctor's Dream
display.summary_short: A Shabbos-observant doctor in Vitebsk dreams of a tzaddik who tells him to travel to save a life. Later, in Lubavitch, he recognizes the man from his dream: the Rebbe Rashab.
display.summary_long: The storyteller opens with the Rebbe's teaching that in earlier times a Rebbe gave a brachah to whoever asked, but now the Rebbeim give brachos even without being asked; we only need to receive them by doing what the Rebbe asks, such as learning Torah, doing mitzvos and learning Rambam every day. The story: the Rebbe Rashab often sent sick people to Dr. Lieberman of Vitebsk, a G-d-fearing doctor who taught Ein Yaakov in shul and avoided traveling on Shabbos, walking to patients when he had to. One Shabbos afternoon he dreams of a striking tzaddik with a red beard who tells him that when a life is in danger, the Torah requires him to travel. Waking, he washes negel vasser, and the storyteller explains washing after a daytime nap. A farmer is at the door: his daughter is critically ill. The doctor rides out at once and nurses her back to health. Soon after he is called to a patient in Lubavitch, goes in to meet the Rebbe Rashab for the first time, and freezes in astonishment at the face he sees.
display.lesson: The Rebbeim give their brachos even before we ask; we receive them by following their instructions. Saving a life overrides Shabbos, and we wash negel vasser after every sleep.

advisories.note: A farmer's daughter is dangerously ill and recovers.

sources_cited.note: The Rebbe told a secretary that today the Rebbeim give brachos even without being asked.
'So says the Alter Rebbe': negel vasser beside the bed at night; after a daytime nap one may wash at the sink.
